topic: 5.3 Complete/Return — delivering a result to a disconnected caller via A2A push notifications
query: A2A protocol push notification config webhook task completion callback
title: Streaming & Asynchronous Operations - A2A Protocol
snippet: The A2A Server decides when to send a push notification, typically when a task reaches a significant state change (for example, terminal state, input-required, or auth-required).
read: the client typically uses the GetTask RPC method with the taskId from the notification to retrieve the complete, updated Task object, including any new artifacts.
claim: A2A's answer to 'how does a disconnected caller get a result back' is a registered webhook (PushNotificationConfig: url, token, auth) that the server POSTs to on terminal state change, after which the client re-fetches the full Task/artifacts via GetTask -- a concrete completion-delivery mechanism, but scoped to agent-to-agent callers, not a general cross-channel envelope for all five entry doors. a2a-protocol.org is a living/versioned spec page with no single publish date; cited as fetched and verified against raw page bytes on 2026-09-09.

topic: 5.3 Complete/Return — published pattern for replying on the same channel the request specified
query: "return address" pattern reply-to channel request-reply enterprise integration pattern async
title: Return Address - Enterprise Integration Patterns
snippet: How does a replier know where to send the reply?
read: The request message should contain a Return Address that indicates where to send the reply message.
claim: Hohpe & Woolf's Return Address pattern (Enterprise Integration Patterns, 2003 -- older than this record's 2026-03+ recency preference, flagged per the recency rule, but still the canonical citation in current webhook/queue literature) is the published pattern for 'deliver back through the same channel the request arrived on': the requester stamps its own reply destination onto the request so the replier never hard-codes per-caller delivery logic. This is the generic pattern the reference model's five-door completion step would specialize per door (webhook URL, poll token, SSE stream id, queue reply-to, agent callback).

topic: 5.3 Complete/Return — what proves delivery: acknowledgement, at-least-once vs exactly-once, retry-until-acked
query: webhook delivery at-least-once acknowledgement retry until acked 2026
title: At-Least-Once vs. Exactly-Once Webhook Delivery Guarantees
snippet: Webhooks operate on at-least-once delivery. Exactly-once delivery is a proven impossibility in distributed computing, not a feature any vendor can ship.
read: When a webhook sender doesn't receive an acknowledgment, it cannot distinguish between four scenarios: The message was lost in transit The message was delivered, but the acknowledgment was lost The receiver crashed before processing The network is just slow
claim: Proof that a completion notification was delivered is a receiver-returned HTTP 200 acknowledgement; because a missing ack is ambiguous between four loss/success scenarios, current practice retries with exponential backoff until acked rather than achieving true exactly-once, and pushes de-duplication onto the receiver via idempotent processing -- so 'exactly-once' completion delivery is marketed, not actually achievable, per this source. Page dated 2026-01-30 (datePublished), slightly before the 2026-03+ preferred window but the clearest current statement of the ack mechanism found.

topic: 5.3 Complete/Return — current-practice tradeoffs among polling, webhooks, websockets and SSE for returning a result
query: async API result delivery pattern webhook polling SSE tradeoffs 2026
title: Polling vs. Webhooks vs. WebSockets vs. SSE: Choosing the Right Real-Time Architecture - DEV Community
snippet: Automatic reconnection. EventSource reconnects on its own after a network blip, and can resume via a Last-Event-ID header — you don't have to hand-write that logic.
read: Average event-discovery latency is roughly half your polling interval
claim: None of the four mechanisms is a universal answer for a caller that may be disconnected when work finishes: polling trades latency (about half the poll interval) for working against any API; SSE is the only one of the four with a built-in reconnect-and-resume story (Last-Event-ID); webhooks are server-to-server only and cannot reach a browser caller directly; websockets have no built-in catch-up at all. The completion step's delivery mechanism is therefore forced by which of the five entry doors the original request came through, not a single best default. Page dated 2026-08-10 (datePublished), inside the preferred window.

topic: 5.3 Complete/Return — CloudEvents Subscriptions API push/pull delivery modes as a candidate completion-delivery standard
query: CloudEvents Subscriptions API delivery modes push pull spec 2026
title: spec/subscriptions/spec.md at main · cloudevents/spec
snippet: Subscriptions with subscription-manager-initiated delivery ("push"-style) are configured on the subscription manager for delivering events through a communication channel that the subscription manager initiates when events are available for delivery on the subscription.
read: individual deliveries might have to be acknowledged by the consumer.
claim: CloudEvents already standardizes the event envelope (id/source/type/time); its separate, less-adopted Subscriptions API is the piece that would standardize completion delivery itself, naming both push-style (manager-initiated, e.g. webhook) and pull-style (consumer-initiated, e.g. MQTT/AMQP) delivery -- but it leaves acknowledgement to the underlying transport's own QoS/settlement semantics rather than defining a delivery-proof contract once at the CloudEvents layer. CloudEvents gives a shared envelope, not a shared delivery-proof contract. spec.md on the main branch is a living document with no single publish date; cited as fetched and verified against raw markdown bytes on 2026-09-09.

topic: 5.3 Complete/Return — the closest candidate for a completion-envelope standard, and why it does not qualify
query: RFC 9457 async job completion status completedAt correlationId draft
title: draft-ratnawat-httpapi-async-problem-details-00 - Problem Details for Asynchronous Job Failures
snippet: Although the primary motivation is structured error reporting for failed jobs, the extension members are equally useful for communicating successful job outcomes (e.g., a COMPLETED status with timing information).
read: "Problem Details for HTTP APIs" (RFC 9457) provides the envelope; this document defines extension members that fill it with asynchronous-job-specific context.
claim: The nearest candidate for a completion envelope standard -- jobId/jobStatus/completedAt/correlationId as RFC 9457 extension members, explicitly reusable for success outcomes and not just failures -- is draft-ratnawat-httpapi-async-problem-details-00 (revision dated 2026-03-01), but the datatracker page records it as an Expired Internet-Draft, individual submission, with no IESG endorsement or formal standing as of this record's date. No open standard for a completion/result-delivery envelope currently fits; this expired draft is the closest unratified attempt found.

topic: 5.3 Complete/Return — AsyncAPI's request/reply pattern as a second same-channel-return precedent
query: AsyncAPI replyTo correlationId request reply pattern message broker
title: Request/reply pattern | AsyncAPI Initiative for event-driven APIs
snippet: Request/reply is a messaging pattern involving two key components: the requester, which sends a request message, and the replier, responsible for receiving this request and responding with a reply.
claim: AsyncAPI 3.0 formalizes the same Return-Address idea for message-broker channels: an operation declares a reply.channel (confirmed on-page: `reply: channel: $ref: '#/channels/pong'`), and separately a correlationId component whose location is a runtime expression (e.g. `$message.header#/requestId`) pointing at a field in the original request, so the reply is routed back on a channel and matched to its request without the replier hard-coding either -- a second, protocol-level instance of the same-channel-return pattern alongside A2A's webhook config and EIP's Return Address. Docs page is a living tutorial with no single publish date; cited as fetched and verified against raw page bytes on 2026-09-09.
